Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Healthcare Services Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not use your telephone keypad during the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Healthcare Services' financial results for the second quarter 2024. Joining me on the call are David Patel, Chief Executive Officer; Emily Rodriguez, Chief Financial Officer; and Tom Vargas, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Patel.

David Patel:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network of 180 acute care hospitals and over 1,200 ambulatory sites across 22 states, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on four key aspects: overview of key financial performance highlights, trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, operating margin year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, and trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue.

These results demonstrate our ability to navigate industry challenges like labor shortages, reimbursement pressures from CMS updates, and the move to value-based care, while driving growth through procedural recovery and outpatient expansion.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Emily to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Emily Rodriguez:
Thank you, David, and good morning, everyone. As David highlighted, we delivered a strong quarter. Let me walk you through our key financial performance highlights, starting with the top-line numbers and the trends underpinning them, all set against persistent labor pressures from nursing shortages, reimbursement challenges from CMS's inpatient prospective payment system updates, and the shift to value-based care models such as the Medicare Shared Savings Program. Despite these, we achieved robust revenue growth, margin improvements via tight operational controls, and solid advancement on our priorities.

For Q2, total net revenues hit $15.4 billion, reflecting 7.8% growth year-over-year, or 6.2% on a same-facility basis—our ninth consecutive quarter of organic top-line expansion, powered by strong procedural volume recovery and our emphasis on higher-margin outpatient offerings. Net income attributable to Apex shareholders reached $512 million, or $1.45 per diluted share, up 12% from $458 million or $1.29 per share in Q2 2023. Adjusted net income, stripping out litigation settlements and restructuring costs, was $578 million or $1.63 per share, surpassing the midpoint of our guidance.

Adjusted EBITDA, our primary measure of core operations, rose to $2.35 billion, a 9.5% year-over-year increase, with margins expanding 80 basis points to 15.3%. This stands out amid wage inflation—national RN rates up 5-7% according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data—and supply chain costs 3-4% above pre-pandemic norms, as noted by peers like HCA Healthcare and Tenet. Our edge came from volume leverage with 4.8% same-facility adjusted admission growth, pricing strength via 1.4% higher net revenue per adjusted admission, and expense growth limited to 6.1%.

Core hospital metrics, making up 72% of revenues, showed same-facility admissions at 512,000, up 4.8% year-over-year, led by surgical surges: orthopedics up 8.1%, PCI cardiology procedures up 7.4%, neurosurgery up 5.9%. Patient days grew 3.9% to 2.85 million, with length of stay steady at 4.7 days, thanks to efficient throughput from our ApexFlow AI platform now at 85% of facilities. Integrated with Epic EHR, it cut ED wait times 22% and lifted case mix index 1.6% to 1.82 for better acuity pay.

Revenue per admission increased 1.4% to $24,100 same-facility, aided by payer mix: commercial/managed care at 48% of revenues, up from 46%; Medicare 32%; Medicaid 15%. Stronger commercial rates in Texas and Florida stem from multi-year deals with UnitedHealthcare and Blue Cross Blue Shield averaging 4.2% annual hikes. CMS FY2025 IPPS with 2.9% update minus 0.5% productivity is a $120 million annual drag, offset by documentation enhancements.

Outpatient shone, at 28% of revenues and up 12.4% to $4.3 billion; same-facility revenue per visit up 3.1% to $285, driven by 15% ambulatory surgery center growth to 320 sites after a $450 million Southeast ASC tuck-in. Cataracts, colonoscopies, joint injections up 14%, fitting No Surprises Act and site-neutral trends. Behavioral health, 45 freestanding sites, grew 11% to $850 million on 9.2% admission gains and 88% utilization amid mental health demand.

Sunbelt regions led: Southeast (Florida, Georgia, Carolinas; 45% beds) up 9.2% same-facility revenue, 6.5% admissions from migration and electives. Texas (22% EBITDA) up 8.4% despite 1.2-point Medicaid redetermination hit. Midwest (Illinois, Ohio) softer at 3.1% from flu and denials, countered by $150 million capex including Q4 Columbus 200-bed hospital.

Labor costs, 65% of total, up 7.2% to $8.1 billion, tempered by 92% clinical retention (from 87%) via ApexCare incentives and AMN partnerships. Non-labor up 4.6%, drugs/supplies 3.8% via Vizient GPO saving $95 million. AR days at 48, top-tier, with AI revenue cycle post-Change Healthcare cyber issues holding denials under 4% vs. 7% industry.

This supports our High-Growth, High-Margin strategy: $400 million shares repurchased YTD at $68 average, $1.2 billion left; dividend up 8% to $0.48. Capex $2.8-3.0 billion for 10 de novos, 50 ASCs, eyeing 200 bps EBITDA expansion by 2026. Value-based: 35% Medicare in ACO REACH/MSSP, $180 million savings last year.

Q3 outlook: revenues $15.6-15.9 billion, EBITDA $2.40-2.50 billion; full-year revenues $62.5-63.5 billion, EBITDA $9.75-10.05 billion, EPS $6.55-6.75. Watch union risks like Kaiser, Medicare sequestration, but $4.5 billion liquidity helps.

Building on these highlights, let's unpack inpatient versus outpatient volume trends, which are reshaping growth and profitability as we manage the shift to outpatient while defending inpatient acuity amid payer and site-neutral pressures.

Consolidated inpatient admissions were 142,000, down 2.1% year-over-year and flat quarter-over-quarter, due to lower-acuity cases like COPD and pneumonia moving to observation or outpatient infusions. Inpatient days fell 3.2% to 785,000, with length of stay down 1.8 points to 5.5 days. Positively, case mix index rose 2.4% to 1.92 from ortho, neuro, oncology strength, pushing revenue per admission up 4.7% to $14,200.

Outpatient registrations reached 1.82 million, up 8.6% year-over-year and 3.2% sequentially, with surgical procedures up 12.4% in cataracts, colonoscopies, pain management. Revenue per visit rose 5.1% to $1,450 on complex cases like robotic hysterectomies, ablations. Outpatient now 62% of volume mix, from 57% two years ago, matching HCA and Tenet at 65-70%.

Trailing 12 months: inpatient down 4.8%, outpatient up 15.2%, echoing CMS/MedPAC data on 6% national inpatient drop since 2021 from ACO REACH, readmissions program, post-COVID elective catch-up (ortho/general surgery 95% recovered).

Sunbelt (Florida, Texas, Arizona): outpatient +14% from demographics, ASCs in Tampa/Phoenix adding 25,000 procedures, 85% utilization, 35%+ EBITDA vs. 22% hospital ORs. Northeast (PA, NY): inpatient -5.1% from Medicaid redeterminations, No Surprises; outpatient +6% via UnitedHealthcare bundles.

Initiatives: $250 million OR optimization with 100+ da Vinci Xi systems boosting outpatient throughput 18%, turn times to 32 minutes; Epic MyChart telehealth in 75% markets up virtual pre-ops 22%. Inpatient: High-Acuity Retention Program with Cerner analytics prioritizing transplants, sepsis for 3-point CMI lift.

Ahead, inpatient decline eases to 1-2% H2 on chronic/Ozempic/stroke demand; outpatient 8-10% with 15 new ASC JVs like Tenet's USPI, supporting 4-6% revenue growth, 28% outpatient margins vs. 18% inpatient.

Next, operating margins, a core efficiency gauge. For Q2 2024, we posted 8.2%, up 120 basis points year-over-year from 7.0% in Q2 2023, down 50 basis points quarter-over-quarter from 8.7% in Q1. This reflects execution against labor inflation, supplies, CMS FY2025 IPPS 2.7% net DRG hike.

Year-over-year gain from 9.2% revenue growth to $15.4 billion on 6.8% adjusted admissions, ortho/cardio, CMI +1.4% to 1.92, commercial 58% mix from 55%, outpatient surgeries +12%, ASCs 22% procedural revenue like HCA.

Expenses: labor to 49.5% from 52% via Core Workforce Optimization—travel nurses -65%, retention 89%. Supplies 14.8% via Vizient, $45 million savings, BPCI ortho/pharma.

Southeast (Florida/Texas, 42% of 180-hospital footprint): margins +180 bps to 10.1% on demographics, Medicaid tailwinds, lower uncompensated care post-No Surprises. Midwest: -50 bps on denials, fixed by Epic AI coding to 97.5% clean claims.

Quarter-over-quarter: seasonal, no $28 million Q1 Medicare settlement, $15 million Q2 ransomware (now Crowdstrike-secured); core +20 bps. Volumes flat at 512,000 discharges, revenue/admission +2.1% to $24,100.

Ahead of peers (HCA 9.5%, Tenet 6.8%), UnityCare/Palantir optimizes to 4.8:1 ratios, $12 million overtime save; 35% revenue at risk MSSP/CJR, readmits 14.2% vs. 15.9%. Full-year margins 8.0-8.4%, Q3 8.5-8.8% on flu/labor; long-term 9%+ via outpatient, M&A Dallas-Fort Worth, Optum-style JVs.

Finally, payer mix shifts and revenue effects. Full-year 2023: 48% Medicare, 38% commercial/managed/FFS, 10% Medicaid, 4% other. Q2 2024: Medicare 51% (+300 bps YoY), commercial 35% (-300 bps), Medicaid 10%, other 4%; T12M net -1.5 points to government pay.

This hit NRPEA 2.1% to $14,200 from $14,510, contractuals 32% from 30% via IPPS; Medicare $11,500/discharge vs. commercial $18,200 (38% premium); $85 million Q2 top-line drag, offset by 4.2% volume, CMI 1.68 from 1.64.

Drivers: Boomer Medicare swell (CMS: MA 54% by 2026); Sunbelt (60% of 45? wait, 180 hospitals) Medicare +7% on migration/chronic. Medicaid stable in 8 ACA states; commercial squeeze from narrow networks, site-neutral (15% at 110-120% Medicare).

Southeast (Atlanta/Jacksonville): Medicaid 14%, cushioned by payer JVs. Midwest: commercial 42%, MA denials +12% Humana/Centene.

Responses: 80% commercial renewals +4.5% FY25 with TCCC incentives like HCA 5%; VBC 28% revenue (from 22%), 15 Aetna/Cigna bundles +2-3% margins; Apex ACO REACH 120k lives, $22 million 2023 savings to $30 million; Epic/payer integration -18% denials, AR 42 days.

Service shift: ASCs 22 sites (SCA acquisition), 65% commercial, $4,800 NRPEA, outpatient 42% total (+500 bps). Mix stable Medicare 50-52% 2025; guidance 1-2% NRPEA drag offset by volumes/margins.

Net revenue for the quarter was $15.4 billion, up 7.8% compared to last year, driven by patient volumes and payer mix. Operating expenses were $13.3 billion, or 86.4% of net revenue. Net income was $512 million, or $1.45 per share. We're pleased and confident in full-year goals.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to David.

David Patel:
Thank you, Emily. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of labor pressures and nursing shortages on your operations?

David Patel:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, labor remains a key focus. As Emily noted, we've moderated the 7.2% labor cost increase to $8.1 billion through a 92% retention rate, up from 87%, leveraging our ApexCare incentives and alternatives to travel nurses via AMN partnerships. We've reduced travel utilization significantly, aligning with industry moderation, while investing in upskilling for a stable core workforce. This has kept us resilient versus peers facing 5-7% RN inflation, and our 4.8:1 nurse ratios via predictive tools support throughput without burnout.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
What are your expectations for patient volume growth in the next quarter, considering the current environment?

Emily Rodriguez:
Thanks, Maria. We're guiding for moderated inpatient declines of 1-2% in H2, stabilizing on high-acuity from chronics, Ozempic GI issues, and CDC-noted stroke upticks. Outpatient sustains 8-10% growth, with upside from 15 new ASC JVs, pushing consolidated 4-6% revenue. Sunbelt demographics and ASC utilization at 85% give tailwinds, while tech like ApexFlow and da Vinci keeps throughput strong.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim:
On payer mix, how are you mitigating the shift to Medicare and any guidance impacts?

Emily Rodriguez:
Great question, Alex. The 300 bps Medicare uptick to 51% is demographic-driven, but we've countered with 4.5% commercial uplifts on 80% renewals, VBC at 28% revenue generating shared savings, and ASC/high-commercial outpatient at 42% total revenue. NRPEA headwind of 1-2% is more than offset in guidance by volumes and efficiencies; mix stabilizes at 50-52% Medicare through 2025 barring policy shifts.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There are no further questions at this time.

David Patel:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Healthcare Services Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.

Trends in inpatient vs. outpatient volumes

aspect_summary.Overview of key financial performance hi: Q2 total net revenues $15.4B (+7.8% YoY, 6.2% same-facility), net income $512M or $1.45/share (+12% YoY), adjusted EBITDA $2.35B (+9.5% YoY, margin 15.3% +80bps), driven by 4.8% admission growth, 1.4% higher revenue per admission, 12.4% outpatient revenue growth to $4.3B, despite labor and reimbursement pressures.
aspect_summary.Trends in inpatient vs. outpatient volum: Inpatient admissions 142,000 (-2.1% YoY, flat QoQ), days -3.2% to 785,000, LOS down 1.8pts to 5.5 days, offset by CMI +2.4% to 1.92 and revenue/admission +4.7%; outpatient registrations 1.82M (+8.6% YoY, +3.2% QoQ), procedures +12.4%, revenue/visit +5.1% to $1,450, now 62% of volume (up from 57% two years ago); T12M inpatient -4.8%, outpatient +15.2%; H2 inpatient decline eases to 1-2%, outpatient 8-10%.
aspect_summary.Operating margin (YoY and QoQ): Q2 operating margin 8.2%, +120bps YoY from 7.0% in Q2 2023, -50bps QoQ from 8.7% in Q1 2024, driven by revenue growth (+9.2%), labor optimization (49.5% of rev from 52%), supply savings, and outpatient expansion; full-year guidance 8.0-8.4%.
aspect_summary.Trends in payer mix shifts and their imp: Q2 payer mix: Medicare 51% (+300bps YoY from 48%), commercial 35% (-300bps), Medicaid 10%; T12M government pay -1.5pts, causing NRPEA -2.1% to $14,200 and $85M revenue drag; driven by Medicare boomer swell and commercial squeeze; mitigated by 4.5% commercial renewals, VBC savings ($22M in 2023), CMI/volume gains, ASC commercial focus; mix stable at 50-52% Medicare in 2025 with 1-2% NRPEA headwind offset.
